speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin my evaluation of your hypertension, how old are you, and have you been diagnosed with high blood pressure before?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Since he is a 5-year-old with no prior diagnosis, this is likely secondary hypertension. Have you noticed any specific symptoms like headaches, vision changes, or swelling in his legs or face recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Renal Artery Stenosis (likely due to Fibromuscular Dysplasia or congenital narrowing) causing differential blood pressure.

I am impressed by your observation of a blood pressure discrepancy. To confirm this, I need to check your pulse in both arms and examine your abdomen for any bruits or abdominal masses. Please extend your arms and relax for me. While I do that, can you tell me if you have experienced any episodes of fainting, dizziness, or sudden abdominal pain?
